summary: Sarat Sarma specializes in philosophy and Buddhist studies. Sarma earned a PhD at Manipur University (attested 2006) under doctoral supervisor S. Shyamkishore Singh, having also studied under S. Lokendrajit Singh.

Sarath Piyananda Weerasekara works in Buddhist and religious studies. He pursued a PhD in Sinhala Medium at the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies under the doctoral supervision of Deshapriya Gunasena / G. A. Gamini (attested 2026).

Saroja Bhate (born 1942) works in Indology and linguistics. She served as a professor at Savitribai Phule Pune University (~1989–2002) and as Honorary Secretary at the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute (~2002–2006).

Sarva Daman Singh is a scholar in Indology and history and archaeology. He held posts at the University of Queensland, serving as Professor of History (attested 1958) and remaining affiliated there (attested 1987).

Sarvepalli Gopal (1923–2002) was a historian who studied at Mill Hill School, Madras Christian College, Presidency College, Chennai, the University of Madras (~1940–1945), and Balliol College, Oxford (~1945–1951). He held a post at Jawaharlal Nehru University (~1971–1983).

Sarvepalli Radhakrishnan (1888–1975) worked in philosophy, Indology, and religious studies. Educated at Madras Christian College, he held posts at Mysore, Calcutta, Oxford (1936–1952), served as Vice-Chancellor of Andhra and Banaras Hindu Universities, and was Chancellor of Delhi University (1953–1962).

Saswati Mutsuddy works in Buddhist studies and Indology, having studied under Dipak Kumar Barua. She served as an assistant professor in the Department of Pali at the University of Calcutta (attested 2011).

Satiranjan Sen was a scholar of Sinology and Buddhist studies who studied at Peking University and founded Cheen Bharat Sanskriti. He held appointments as a Research Scholar and Junior Research Fellow at Visva-Bharati University.

Satish Chandra (1922–2017) was an Indologist and historian who studied at the University of Allahabad (~1940–1948). He held academic posts at Aligarh Muslim University (~1953–1961) and the University of Rajasthan (~1961–1970).

Satish Chandra Vidyabhusan (1870–1920) was an Indologist, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Krishnagar Government College, Sanskrit College, and Calcutta University under Sarat Chandra Das. He served as Principal of Sanskrit College (~1910–1920).

Satkari Mookerjee (1896–1968) was an Indology, philosophy, and Buddhist studies scholar. He served as Ashutosh Professor of Sanskrit at the University of Calcutta (~1943–1956) and as Director of Nava Nalanda Mahavihara (1955).

Satkari Mukhopadhyaya is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar. He held appointments at the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts as Coordinator of the Kala Kosa Division (attested 1999, 2026).
Satkari Sharma Vangiya is a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He pursued his traditional education under Ramachandra Shastri Vyakaranacharya (also attested under Ramachandra Sastri in 1970).

Satoru Harada (born 1947) works in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, earning an M.A. at the University of Tokyo (attested 1973). He held posts at Toyo Bunko (attested 1978), Eastern Institute (attested 1982), and Kokushikan University (attested 2010–2015).
Satoru Noriyama works in Buddhist studies and studied under Esho Mikogami. He held teaching posts at Osaka University of Foreign Studies (attested 1995) and Ryukoku University (attested 2003, 2013).
Satoshi Fujiwara is a Buddhist studies scholar who served as a researcher at the Shinran Buddhist Center (attested 2015) and as a lecturer at the Otani Academic Society (attested 2026).
Satoshi Hayashima specializes in Buddhist studies. He was a research student at Ryukoku University (attested 2013–2014) and later served as a lecturer there (attested 2015–2017).

Satoshi Hiraoka (born 1960) works in Buddhist studies and Indology. Educated at Bukkyo University and the University of Michigan, he held positions at Bukkyo University (~1993) and Kyoto Bunkyo University, where he became professor (1996) and president (2014).
Satoshi Ito (born 1961) is a scholar in Japanology, religious studies, and Buddhist studies who studied at Waseda University. He served as a professor at Ibaraki University (~2003).
Satoshi Kono (born 1954) is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Sinology. He earned a doctorate in literature at the University of Tokyo and served as a professor at Kogakkan University (2000).
